row.title: Dido
row.citation_text: British Museum Collections Online identifies Dido/Elissa as a mythological figure and legendary founder/queen of Carthage; this supports retaining only an explicitly legendary traditional rulership assertion.

row.title: Senones
row.citation_text: Edward Togo Salmon, Oxford Classical Dictionary, Senones (2016): identifies the Senones as a Gallic tribe/political community in Italy and notes the literary tradition associating them with the Gallic band that captured Rome.

row.title: Herodotus, Histories, Book 1, 205–215
row.citation_text: Herodotus, Histories Book 1, Perseus Digital Library: presents Tomyris as queen/ruler of the Massagetae and narrates the traditional conflict with Cyrus; ATLAS preserves this as source-qualified ancient testimony.

row.title: Shiji — Biography of Tian Dan and Tian Heng
row.citation_text: Sima Qian, Shiji, Tian Dan biography, Chinese Text Project: records Tian Heng's Qi kingship/sovereign posture and his refusal to submit after Han unification.

row.title: Journey of Faith: Haj Pilgrimage in the Malay Archipelago before the 20th Century
row.citation_text: National Library Board Singapore, BiblioAsia: places the founding of the Kingdom of Malacca around 1400 and discusses Parameswara as its founder, with conversion tradition by 1414.

row.title: Time to revisit our history textbooks - Vice President
row.citation_text: Press Information Bureau, Government of India: states that Azad Hind was formed as a provisional government in 1943 and identifies Subhas Chandra Bose as head of state and leader of the INA.
